sections.h2: What kind of place is Avon, Ohio for a home seller?
sections.html:
Avon is a Lorain County suburb in the Cleveland area, and most of its homes are owner-occupied. The city has 20.79 square miles of land, nearly twice the area of neighboring Avon Lake, and Census estimates put it at 25,611 residents for 2025.

The land began as Township Number 7 in the Western Reserve, with its first permanent settlers arriving in 1814. The township was organized in 1818 as Xeuma, later became Troy Township, and took the name Avon Township when Lorain County formed in 1824. A post office opened in 1825, the area incorporated as a village in 1917, and it became the City of Avon in 1961.

Growth has been steady. Wikipedia's census table shows 11,446 residents in 2000, 21,193 in 2010 and 24,847 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate of 25,611 is about 3% above the 2020 base.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Avon homes?
sections.html:
Home values run high in Avon. In the 2020 to 2024 data, 88.3% of homes are owner-occupied and the median value is $395,900. The 9,502 households average 2.63 people, rent has a median of $1,796, and monthly owner costs come to $2,471 with a mortgage and $818 without.

  • In the 2020 census, 41.5% of households had children under 18.
  • Married couples headed 64.2% of households, and the median age was 40.7.
  • The city had 9,208 housing units, with 4.2% vacant.

Those figures describe buyers who expect a move-in ready house. A seller who cannot take on repairs, or who faces a divorce, a relocation or an estate, may find a direct purchase simpler than preparing the house for the open market.

sections.h2: Where do Avon property tax dollars go?
sections.html:
Most of an Avon tax bill pays for the schools. The city's welcome packet divides the 2025 tax year as shown below, and the city itself receives 10.12% of the total.

How the 2025 Avon property tax bill was divided, per the city's welcome packet
RecipientShare of the bill
Avon Schools66.43%
Lorain County19.18%
City of Avon10.12%
Lorain JVSD3.63%
Lorain Health0.64%

The same packet says Avon levies a 1.95% municipal income tax, with a credit of up to 1.7% for residents who work in another city, administered by the Regional Income Tax Agency. A buyer weighing Avon against a nearby town will look at both figures.

The Lorain County Treasurer runs an optional monthly escrow plan for tax payments, and the treasurer's site posts the current due dates, which have moved when the state changed the schedule. Your title company will prorate the tax between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: Which Avon schools and amenities do buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Avon Local School District serves the city. Its buildings are the Early Learning Center for preschool and kindergarten, Avon East Elementary for grades 1 and 2, Heritage Elementary for grades 3 through 5, Avon Middle School for grades 6 through 8, and Avon High School. Avon Middle School was named a Blue Ribbon school for 2020 by the U.S. Department of Education. Private options the city lists include Holy Trinity School, St. Mary School and Avon Montessori Academy.

The library is a branch of the Lorain Public Library, and a 16,000 square foot expansion opened in January 2023. The city runs parks along Detroit Road and Schwartz Road, an aquatic facility, a senior center and a dog park, and the Lake Erie Crushers play on Baseball Boulevard. Trash goes out on Mondays with Republic Services, and the city handles fall leaf pickup. The Service Department clears snow on more than 250 lane miles in a set order of main, secondary and residential streets. Avon belongs to the Northeast Ohio Public Energy Council for gas and electric supply, which a household can stay with or leave.

sections.h2: What Avon rules affect a house you plan to sell?
sections.html:
The Avon Building and Zoning Departments share City Hall at 36600 Detroit Road. The city tells residents to contact the Building Department for a pool, irrigation, deck, patio, shed, finished basement, fence, new roof, siding or any addition, and says contractors must be registered. Check that each of those projects at your house has a closed permit.

Avon runs on a mayor and council form of government, with seven part-time council members (three at large and four by ward). Work sessions are held on the first and third Mondays and regular meetings on the second and fourth Mondays at 7:30 p.m., so a seller who needs a zoning question aired in public knows when to attend.

  • Utilities: water and sewer bills go out monthly and are due on the 25th, and meters report actual daily use. Call the Utilities Department to move service out of your name.
  • Sprinklers: an in-ground system needs an approved backflow device, tested each year before June 30, with results sent to the city.
  • Short-term rentals: a 2021 ordinance extending a moratorium said the zoning code bars uses it does not list, and that short-term rentals are not listed. Ask the Zoning Department whether anything has changed before you market the house to an investor.

Avon also keeps a Do Not Knock list, and an address stays registered for three years. A seller who is tired of unsolicited offers can ask the city about it.

sections.h2: How does the Ohio paperwork work for an Avon seller?
sections.html:
Ohio law has the seller of a residence with up to four units complete the state disclosure form and deliver it to the buyer (ORC 5302.30). Estate fiduciary sales and transfers to relatives are among the exceptions. If the form arrives after the contract is signed, the buyer has three business days to cancel in writing.

The owner must sign the deed before a notary or another official listed in ORC 5301.01. The deed is then filed with the county recorder, and ORC 5301.25 treats an unrecorded deed as fraudulent against a later purchaser who did not know of it. Before recording, the deed passes through the Lorain County Auditor, which accepts conveyances only in person or by e-file, wants typed forms and returns anything incomplete. County staff cannot fill out the forms, so let the title company file them.

sections.h2: When is a cash sale the better choice in Avon?
sections.html:
A cash sale suits a seller who values a firm closing date over a top price. In a high-value suburb, a listing can draw strong offers, but it also brings staging, showings and repair requests from the buyer.

Work out the net from each route. Add agent fees, repair costs, mortgage payments, taxes and utilities for the weeks a listing may take, and set that total against a direct offer. Get the offer in writing with a closing date, and keep a copy of your signed disclosure form.

faqs.q: Can I rent my Avon house short term before I sell?
faqs.a: Check with the Zoning Department first. A 2021 city ordinance said short-term rentals are not a listed use in the residential districts and are therefore prohibited, so ask whether the rule has changed.

faqs.q: Who processes the deed for an Avon sale?
faqs.a: The Lorain County Auditor processes the transfer and the county recorder files the deed. The auditor takes conveyances in person or by e-file only, and a title company normally handles both steps.

faqs.q: What share of an Avon tax bill goes to the schools?
faqs.a: Avon Schools received 66.43% of the 2025 tax year bill, according to the city's welcome packet. Lorain County received 19.18% and the city 10.12%.

faqs.q: Do I need to disclose problems when I sell in Avon?
faqs.a: Yes, on the Ohio disclosure form for homes with up to four units. It covers water, sewer, structure and known defects, and a buyer who gets it late can rescind within three business days.

faqs.q: Which permits should be closed before I sell in Avon?
faqs.a: Any permit for a deck, pool, shed, fence, roof, siding, finished basement or addition. Ask the Building Department at City Hall about open permits and unfinished inspections.
